answer: Sybil swarms are cheap to spawn but costly to keep consistent. A network can ask each identity to commit a hashed note every epoch, then later reveal a randomly chosen older one. Fake accounts that wander in and out, or that draw on one operator's shared river of output, break their chain of reveals. Like a crystal growing layer by layer, an identity earns credibility only from an unbroken record that can't be backfilled after the fact.
